question: Which summit in July 2025 emphasised Global South cooperation under Brazil’s chairmanship?
solution:
The correct answer is __**BRICS Summit**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Brazil** officially assumed the **chairmanship** of the **BRICS** group for the year **2025**, succeeding **Russia**.
 
• The **BRICS Summit** held in **July 2025** placed a significant emphasis on **Global South cooperation**, reflecting **Brazil's** long-standing foreign policy priority of fostering ties among developing nations.
 
• Under **Brazil’s** leadership, the summit focused on critical issues such as **inequality reduction**, **combating hunger**, and the **reform of international financial institutions** like the **IMF** and **World Bank** to better represent emerging economies.
 
• The **2025 Summit** served as a platform for the recently expanded **BRICS+** members to align their strategies on **climate action** and **sustainable development** ahead of **COP30**, which **Brazil** is also scheduled to host.
 
• The emphasis on the **Global South** was intended to strengthen the collective bargaining power of nations in **Africa**, **Asia**, and **Latin America** within the global geopolitical landscape. ***Hence, the correct answer is the BRICS Summit.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **BRICS Expansion:** Originally composed of **Brazil, Russia, India, China, and South Africa**, the group expanded in **January 2024** to include **Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, and the United Arab Emirates**, enhancing its representation of the **Global South**.
 
• **Global South:** This term refers to various countries often characterized as "developing" or "newly industrialized," primarily located in the **Southern Hemisphere**. It represents a shift in global economic power toward **non-Western** nations.
 
• **G7 Summit:** The **Group of Seven** consists of advanced economies including the **USA, UK, France, Germany, Italy, Canada, and Japan**. Unlike **BRICS**, it represents the **Global North** and traditional economic powers.
 
• **APEC Summit:** The **Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation** is a regional economic forum established in **1989** to leverage the growing interdependence of the **Asia-Pacific**. It includes **21 member economies** but is not focused exclusively on the **Global South**.
 
• **ASEAN Summit:** The **Association of Southeast Asian Nations** is a regional organization that promotes economic, political, and security cooperation among its **10 member states** in **Southeast Asia**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **New Development Bank (NDB):** Often called the **BRICS Bank**, this institution is headquartered in **Shanghai** and provides financing for infrastructure projects in **BRICS** and other emerging economies, acting as an alternative to the **World Bank**.
 
• **Rotating Chairmanship:** The **BRICS chairmanship** rotates annually among its members. During its **2025** tenure, **Brazil** pushed for the use of **local currencies** in international trade to reduce dependence on the **US Dollar**.
 
• **Geopolitical Influence:** Collectively, **BRICS** members represent over **40% of the world's population** and a significant portion of global **GDP**, making their summits crucial for global economic governance.
 
• **Strategic Themes:** Brazil's **2025** agenda also included **energy transition** and **digital transformation**, aiming to bridge the digital divide between the **Global North** and **Global South**.
